title: Define prefix/KV cache metrics + tags (names, labels, bucketing, acceptance tests)
creator: Talia Benson
description:
## Context
We’re standardizing prefix cache + KV cache telemetry across runtime + gateway + ingestion so SRE/Platform can reliably debug cache regressions and we can feed a first-pass recommendations MVP ("increase hit-rate").

This ticket finalizes:
- metric definitions (hit/miss semantics, partial hits, multi-turn chat attribution)
- metric names (aligned with cache observability standards)
- label set + allowlists (cardinality budget)
- bucketing rules (prompt/prefill/decode token histograms)
- acceptance tests (runtime + ingestion/guard rails)

## References
- ADR: `sources/confluence/architecture-and-standards/decision-records/adr-prefix-kv-cache-hit-rate-definition.json`
- Naming/cardinality policy: `sources/confluence/architecture-and-standards/observability-standards/cache-metrics-naming-and-cardinality-policy.json`
- Runtime telemetry architecture: `sources/confluence/eng-serving-runtime/runtime-architecture/kv-cache-telemetry-overview.json`
- Dashboard spec: `sources/confluence/eng-platform/dashboards-and-alerts/cache-hit-rate-dashboards-spec.json`
- Linear follow-ups:
  - ENG-4822 implement counters/histograms in runtime
  - ENG-4823 gateway route/model context tags
  - ENG-4824 dashboards + alerts
  - ENG-4825 recommendations batch job MVP

## Goals / non-goals
### Goals
- Stable metric contract for at least the next 2 releases (avoid breaking dashboards).
- Joinable dimensions that match how we operate: by model, route, deployment_mode, region, request-shape (buckets).
- Avoid cardinality blowups (no tenant_id; no raw prompt; no arbitrary route strings).
- Semantics that hold under streaming retries + continuous batching.

### Non-goals
- Designing a new eviction policy.
- Full customer-facing recommendations UX.

## Final metric definitions (ADR-aligned)
### Key concepts
- **Prefix cache**: caches prefill results for a canonicalized prefix (prompt/template); reuse means we can skip some portion of prefill.
- **KV cache**: per-request decode cache state; in practice we measure reuse effectiveness and pressure/evictions that reduce reuse.

### Hit / miss semantics
- **prefix hit**: any reuse of cached prefix tokens during prefill for a request (i.e., reused_tokens > 0).
- **prefix miss**: request opted into prefix caching but reused_tokens == 0.
- **partial hit**: reused_tokens in (0, prefill_tokens). This is not a separate counter; encoded via histograms + reused token ratio panels.
- **attribution for multi-turn chat**: metrics are emitted per request attempt; request-shape buckets capture prompt/prefill/decode size.
- **streaming retries**: only count once per logical request_id attempt. Retries should be de-duped by runtime instrumentation (tracked in ENG-4822/PR-18428).

### Miss reasons taxonomy (stable enum)
Single label `miss_reason` on miss counters where applicable:
- `capacity` (cache full / no admission)
- `ttl_expired`
- `policy_disabled` (route/model/deployment config)
- `hash_mismatch` (canonicalization mismatch; prompt changed)
- `version_mismatch` (model version incompatible / pinned version changed)

Note: `miss_reason` is **not** emitted on hits and is **not** used for high-frequency histograms.

## Metric names (final)
Naming principle: `redwood.cache.<cache_type>.<noun>_<unit>` with counters `_total`, histograms `_bucket` + `_sum` + `_count` (exporter-dependent).

### Prefix cache
1) `redwood.cache.prefix.requests_total` (counter)
- increment once per request that is eligible for prefix caching (policy enabled, supported route/mode).

2) `redwood.cache.prefix.hits_total` (counter)
- increment once per eligible request where reused_tokens > 0.

3) `redwood.cache.prefix.misses_total` (counter)
- increment once per eligible request where reused_tokens == 0.
- labels include `miss_reason`.

4) `redwood.cache.prefix.reused_tokens_total` (counter)
- total number of prefill tokens satisfied via prefix cache reuse.

5) `redwood.cache.prefix.prefill_tokens_total` (counter)
- total number of prefill tokens computed for eligible requests (including those later deemed wasted).

6) `redwood.cache.prefix.reuse_depth_tokens` (histogram)
- observed reused token count per request (bucketed); used to see partial-hit distribution.

7) `redwood.cache.prefix.wasted_prefill_tokens_total` (counter)
- definition: prefill tokens computed that did not contribute to subsequent decode due to prefix miss/eviction/pressure effects.
- emitted only for eligible requests; **no prompt identifiers**.

### KV cache / eviction / pressure
8) `redwood.cache.kv.evictions_total` (counter)
- labels include `eviction_reason` (stable enum maintained by runtime; do not include object ids).

9) `redwood.cache.kv.pressure_bytes` (gauge)
- instantaneous bytes in use / pressure indicator sampled at a fixed interval (runtime-owned cadence).

10) `redwood.cache.kv.reuse_effective_tokens_total` (counter)
- token-level effectiveness signal (implementation-defined but stable definition documented in runtime overview); used to correlate with hit-rate.

11) `redwood.cache.kv.admission_denied_total` (counter)
- increment when cache admission is denied due to capacity/policy.

## Required labels (allowed everywhere)
These labels must be present for all cache metrics emitted from runtime:
- `deployment_mode`: `hosted` | `dedicated` | `private`
- `region`: short region code (e.g., `us-east-1`, `eu-west-1`)
- `model_id`: Redwood canonical model identifier (e.g., `llama-3-70b-instruct`)
- `model_version`: Redwood version id (not a hash of weights; use control-plane id)

## Allowed optional labels (strict allowlist)
Only apply where noted (to manage series count).

### Route context (high value, controlled)
- `route_id`: Redwood route identifier from gateway allowlist
  - must be a bounded set per workspace (ingestion will drop if not allowlisted)
  - not a free-form string; no user-supplied route names

### Request shape bucketing (low cardinality)
- `prompt_len_bucket`: bucketed input prompt token count
- `prefill_tokens_bucket`: bucketed prefill token count
- `decode_tokens_bucket`: bucketed decoded token count

Bucket set (shared across prefix/KV metrics): `0-32`, `33-128`, `129-256`, `257-512`, `513-1024`, `1025-2048`, `2049-4096`, `4097+`

### Reason labels (only on specific counters)
- `miss_reason`: only on `...prefix.misses_total`
- `eviction_reason`: only on `...kv.evictions_total`

## Explicitly forbidden labels (do not emit)
- `tenant_id`, `workspace_id`, `org_id` (cardinality + privacy)
- raw `prompt_hash`, `prompt`, or any content-derived identifier that can be joined back to content
- `request_id` (metrics), `trace_id` (metrics)
- `host_id` / `pod` labels for these metrics (use traces/logs for per-host debugging)

## Sampling & cardinality constraints
- Default runtime sampling for high-frequency events: **1.0 for request-level counters**, **0.1 for token-level/high-volume metrics** (exact knobs owned by runtime; must be configurable per env).
- Ingestion cardinality guardrails (Telemetry):
  - drop metrics with forbidden labels
  - enforce `route_id` allowlist
  - cap active series per metric per region (see budget sheet; tracked under ENG-4825/ingestion PR)

## Acceptance criteria
### Spec acceptance
- [x] ADR referenced and aligned on hit/miss semantics, streaming retry behavior, and partial-hit representation.
- [x] Metric names conform to cache naming standards.
- [x] Label set is explicitly enumerated (required/optional/forbidden) and matches cardinality budget.

### Implementation acceptance (must be validated by ENG-4822/4823)
- Runtime emits the required labels on all cache metrics.
- Runtime never emits forbidden labels (unit test / linter).
- `route_id` propagation is joinable across gateway + runtime metrics (same id + version semantics).

### Test plan acceptance
1) **Runtime integration test** (new): repeated prompts across two requests must yield:
   - `requests_total` increments by 2
   - at least one `hits_total` increment (after warm cache)
   - `reused_tokens_total` > 0 for the hit request
   - miss reason is set on misses

2) **Streaming retry regression test**: retry should not double count request-level metrics.

3) **Batched prefill correctness**: continuous batching should not attribute hits across different logical requests incorrectly.

4) **Ingestion guard tests** (Telemetry):
   - metrics with forbidden labels are dropped
   - non-allowlisted `route_id` is dropped/aggregated to `route_id=other` (per policy)

## Owners / reviewers
- Runtime instrumentation: Omar El-Sayed / Samir Qureshi
- Metrics schema + ingestion policy: Nadia Rahman / Caleb Johnson
- Dashboard needs + alerting constraints: Allison Grant / Sean Gallagher
- Privacy review: Marcus Lin

## Open questions (resolved)
- Q: Do we need separate counters for partial hits?
  - A: No; partial hit distribution comes from `reuse_depth_tokens` histogram and derived ratios.

- Q: Can we tag by tenant for support triage?
  - A: Not in metrics. Use logs/traces with access controls; metrics remain aggregated and privacy-safe.

- Q: How do we handle model rollouts?
  - A: Tag `model_version` and include `version_mismatch` miss reason so dashboards can isolate rollouts.

## Deliverable
This ticket is complete when the definitions above are treated as the contract for ENG-4822/4823/4824 and linked from the runtime internal README.
comments: 2025-03-04 (Talia Benson): Created as part of sprint alignment. Please treat this as the source of truth for metric names/labels before we ship dashboards. Links: ADR + naming policy in Confluence.

2025-03-05 (Allison Grant): SRE request: we need breakdowns by model_version and region at minimum. Also please ensure no host-level labels; those blow up and aren’t actionable at fleet level. For miss reasons, keep taxonomy stable (don’t overfit to implementation details).

2025-03-06 (Omar El-Sayed): Proposed splitting prefix vs KV names under `redwood.cache.*` to keep dashboards consistent. Also called out streaming retries: runtime will dedupe request-level metrics by logical request attempt; see bug we hit last quarter.

2025-03-06 (Nadia Rahman): Telemetry feedback: hard no on tenant/workspace labels. OK with route_id only if we enforce an allowlist at ingestion and cap active series. Added explicit forbidden label list to the spec to make enforcement testable.

2025-03-07 (Sean Gallagher): Alerting concern: we’ll want miss_reason to interpret hit-rate drops without paging on workload shifts. But please do NOT put miss_reason on histograms (too many series). This spec matches that.

2025-03-08 (Marcus Lin): Privacy review note: do not emit prompt hashes or any deterministic content-derived ids in metrics. Bucketing is fine. Traces can include span annotations but must not include raw prompts; keep that in PR-18432 scope.

2025-03-10 (Caleb Johnson): Ingestion guardrails plan: drop forbidden labels, enforce route_id allowlist, and cap series per metric per region. If route_id violates allowlist, aggregate to `route_id=other` to preserve totals for SLO math.

2025-03-11 (Noah Patel): Partial-hit semantics look good. Make sure the runtime integration test covers batched prefill; we saw misattribution there. Also +1 to keeping `pressure_bytes` as a sampled gauge rather than a per-request label.

2025-03-12 (Nadia Rahman): Marking Done. Spec finalized and aligned with ADR + naming policy. ENG-4822/4823 can implement against this contract; dashboard PR should reference these exact names/labels.
